summary: In the Song’s garden the lover names saffron alongside nard, fragrant cane and cinnamon.

senses.definition: An aromatic plant named among the prized spices of the garden.

evidence.note: Saffron follows nard in the list of fragrant plants. No preparation or dyeing process is described.

evidence.locator: K00385, with variant כּוּרְקְמָא; Shabbat 110a on the garden crocus

cognates.gloss: saffron, also other yellow dye plants

evidence.locator: p. 2293, n32397, kurkum in the entry for ġumra; compare p. 2891, n41129 on yellow dye roots
armep x000034000, kurkanû, also written kulkanû

note: The indexed word has one token and no assigned root key. כרכמ follows its attested consonants. The Aramaic and Syriac forms support the garden-plant identification. The ultimate source and direction of borrowing among the similar spice names remain uncertain.
